correctness.summary: The affine-disk argument is correct. Under the change of variables zeta=A^T xi, the squared Fourier transform of the disk indicator is radial, so the relevant Fourier-mass fractions are exactly angular fractions determined by the two rows of A^{-T}. If their angle is alpha, the sign-disagreement wedges have total angle 2 alpha, which gives the displayed 4(1-alpha/pi) and 4 alpha/pi normalized squared defects. For the diagonal ellipse, alpha=pi-2 arctan(epsilon), hence the exact defect sqrt((8/pi) arctan(epsilon)). The truncated-strip asymptotic also checks independently: with A(t)=integral_t^infinity sin^2(p)/p^2 dp=1/(2t)+O(t^-2), the middle range 1<t<epsilon^-1 contributes (epsilon^2/2) log(1/epsilon)+O(epsilon^2) to the one-quadrant integral; after the two bad quadrants, multiplier factor 4, and |V_epsilon|=4 epsilon, this yields exactly (4/pi^2) epsilon log(1/epsilon)+O(epsilon) for the normalized squared defect.

limitations: No optimality is established among all bounded sets, convex sets, or sets with fixed eccentricity.
The sharp logarithmic asymptotic is specific to the displayed truncated-strip family.
The motivating preprint is very recent, so unindexed concurrent observations cannot be excluded.

originality.summary: Abakumov-Domelevo-Petermichl-Poltoratski (arXiv:2609.15155) already establish finite-measure indicator approximate eigenvectors and the truncated-strip construction. Current searches through 2026-09-29 did not locate the all-ellipse angular identity, the smooth strictly convex log-free family, or the explicit leading constant for the strip leakage. Because the source preprint is only weeks old and the ellipse calculation is elementary once one exploits radial disk Fourier energy, priority is supported only narrowly for these explicit refinements.

scientific_value.summary: The result separates two phenomena that the motivating example leaves entangled: the logarithm is sharp for that hard truncated strip, but it is not intrinsic to bounded continuous indicator quasi-eigenvectors. The exact ellipse formula supplies a simple smooth strictly convex benchmark and the strip calculation turns an upper estimate into a sharp asymptotic.
